evals.prompt:
I just finished planning a task management app. The stack is React 18 with TypeScript on the frontend, Express.js API, and PostgreSQL. Here's the plan:

## Features
- Dashboard showing all projects with task counts and progress bars
- Task board view (Kanban-style with drag and drop columns: To Do, In Progress, Review, Done)
- Task detail modal with title, description, assignee, due date, priority, labels, and comments
- Project settings page for managing members and project metadata

## Data Models
- User: id, email, name, avatarUrl, role (admin/member), createdAt
- Project: id, name, description, ownerId (FK to User), color, isArchived, createdAt, updatedAt
- ProjectMember: id, projectId (FK), userId (FK), role (owner/editor/viewer), joinedAt
- Task: id, projectId (FK), title, description, status (enum: todo/in_progress/review/done), priority (enum: low/medium/high/critical), assigneeId (FK to User, nullable), dueDate (nullable), position (int for ordering within column), createdById (FK to User), createdAt, updatedAt
- Label: id, projectId (FK), name, color
- TaskLabel: taskId (FK), labelId (FK) - junction table
- Comment: id, taskId (FK), authorId (FK to User), body, createdAt, updatedAt

## Architecture
- Frontend: src/components (common + feature folders), src/hooks, src/services, src/store (Zustand), src/types, src/pages
- Backend: src/routes, src/controllers, src/services, src/models, src/middleware, src/utils
- Repository pattern for data access
- JWT auth with refresh tokens
- WebSocket for real-time task updates on the board

Please review this plan before we start building.
evals.expected_output: A single index.html with 4 tabs: Mockups (with sub-nav for dashboard, kanban board, task detail modal, project settings), Data Models (Mermaid ER + entity cards for all 7 entities + enums + indexes), Architecture (folder tree + module diagram + pattern cards for repository pattern, JWT auth, WebSocket), and Concerns.

evals.prompt:
We just planned out a REST API for an inventory management system. No frontend — it's API-only, consumed by a mobile app built by another team. Here's what we planned:

## Entities
- Warehouse: id (uuid), name, address, latitude, longitude, managerId (FK to Staff), capacity, isActive, createdAt
- Staff: id (uuid), email, firstName, lastName, role (enum: admin/manager/picker/viewer), warehouseId (FK, nullable - admins aren't tied to one), hiredAt, isActive
- Product: id (uuid), sku (unique), name, description, category (enum: electronics/clothing/food/furniture/other), weight, dimensions (jsonb), minStockLevel, createdAt
- InventoryItem: id (uuid), productId (FK), warehouseId (FK), quantity, location (aisle-shelf-bin format string), lastCountedAt, updatedAt
- StockMovement: id (uuid), inventoryItemId (FK), type (enum: inbound/outbound/transfer/adjustment), quantity (positive or negative), reason, performedById (FK to Staff), sourceWarehouseId (FK, nullable), destinationWarehouseId (FK, nullable), createdAt
- AuditLog: id (uuid), entityType, entityId, action (enum: create/update/delete), changes (jsonb), performedById (FK to Staff), createdAt

## Architecture
- .NET 8 Web API with Clean Architecture (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API layers)
- CQRS with MediatR for command/query separation
- EF Core 8 with PostgreSQL
- FluentValidation for request validation
- Serilog for structured logging

## Key decisions
- Soft deletes via isActive flag on Warehouse and Staff
- StockMovement is append-only (immutable audit trail)
- Composite unique index on InventoryItem(productId, warehouseId) — one record per product per warehouse
- All quantities tracked as integers (no decimals)

Review this plan for me.
evals.expected_output: A single index.html with 3 tabs (no Mockups tab since there's no UI): Data Models (Mermaid ER + entity cards for all 6 entities + 4 enums + indexes including composite unique), Architecture (Clean Architecture layers + CQRS pattern cards + module diagram), and Concerns.

evals.prompt:
Here's the plan for our analytics dashboard. It's a Next.js 14 app with a Python FastAPI backend and ClickHouse for the analytics database (plus PostgreSQL for user/config data).

## Screens
- Overview dashboard: KPI cards (total revenue, active users, conversion rate, avg session duration) + line chart for revenue over time + bar chart for top products + recent activity feed
- Funnel analysis page: configurable funnel steps, funnel visualization chart, conversion rates between steps, date range picker
- User segments page: segment builder with AND/OR conditions on user properties, segment list with member counts, segment comparison chart

## Data Models (PostgreSQL)
- Organization: id, name, slug, plan (enum: free/pro/enterprise), createdAt
- User: id, orgId (FK), email, name, role (enum: admin/analyst/viewer), lastLoginAt, createdAt
- Dashboard: id, orgId (FK), name, isDefault, layout (jsonb), createdAt, updatedAt
- SavedReport: id, dashboardId (FK), createdById (FK to User), name, type (enum: kpi/chart/funnel/segment), config (jsonb), position, createdAt, updatedAt
- Segment: id, orgId (FK), name, conditions (jsonb), memberCount (cached int), lastComputedAt, createdById (FK to User), createdAt

## Data Models (ClickHouse — read-only from app perspective)
- events: event_id, org_id, user_external_id, event_name, event_properties (Map), timestamp, session_id
- user_profiles: org_id, user_external_id, properties (Map), first_seen, last_seen

## Architecture
- Next.js App Router with server components for initial data load
- Recharts for data visualization
- FastAPI backend with async SQLAlchemy (PostgreSQL) and clickhouse-connect (ClickHouse)
- Redis for caching expensive ClickHouse queries
- Background worker (Celery) for segment computation

Let me review before we build.
evals.expected_output: A single index.html with 4 tabs: Mockups (sub-nav for overview dashboard with charts, funnel analysis, user segments), Data Models (both PostgreSQL and ClickHouse entities, Mermaid ER for PG relationships, entity cards for all 7 entities across both databases), Architecture (Next.js + FastAPI + dual DB folder structure, module diagram showing frontend→API→PG/ClickHouse/Redis/Celery flow, pattern cards), and Concerns (likely flagging dual-database complexity, caching strategy, ClickHouse query performance).
